title: Add AMR codec support
description:
The AMR (Adaptive Multi Rate) codec is used in a variety of 3GPP cellular
networks. Its encapsulation into RTP is specified in RFC 4867.  Wireshark
does have a AMR dissector, but has historically not carried any plugins for
decoding AMR audio due to perceived fear of patent infringement.

Based on my understanding, AMR patentes should have all expired by 2019:
* it was first published/specified in GSM TS 06.90 Rel 7.0.0 released in
  February 1999
* patents needed to be filed *before* any publication
* patents are granted for 20 years *from the filing date*

Furthermore, the actual voice codec is implemented in an external, shared
library (libopencore-amr) which is part of all standard Linux distributions for
several years by now (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE), so they all
appear to consider AMR as something safe to ship to their users.

So let's attempt to finally get (narrow band) AMR support merged to wireshark, please

I really do not know much about patents, but noticed that the patent referenced in this link (https://patents.google.com/patent/US7403892B2/en) may have been extended to 2024-05-08 ?  I can't readily tell if this MR usage of the library is affected by it.

The patent you are referencing describes a "method for efficient adaptive mode selecting".  That is an optimization of the way how the *encoder* selects the AMR mode.  So it doesn't cover the AMR codec itself, but how to more efficiently select the mode.  Furthermore, as wireshark is decoding only, it doesn't select any modes at all.

I'm not familiar with that.  I'd somehow be surprised if a codec plugin should also make changes to the main program, which may or may not use the plugin. The plugin might not be compiled, or it might not be present at runtime.  So whatever you display at other parts in wireshark would need to depend on whether or not the plugin is loaded at runtime?
I meant rather epan_gather_compile_info() in epan/epan.c, but as you noted it doesn't refer to build flags that are only used for plugins.

Looking back at my version of this and some notes I made (and it was a long time ago)...

I was registering for "AMR-NB" or "AMR-WB" for VoLTE, as those were set in the SDP.  For WB, the get_frequency callback had to return 16000.

For 3G, where the stream wasn't really being setup properly (from the RANAP) I was just (sadly) matching with "RTPType-96".  Though there was some confusion about the frequency for NB (might have been a local bug, but I had to choose between correct pitch and timing of playback - with or without jitter buffer).

This patch is intentionally about classic narrow-band AMR only.  

Note that the patent situation on wiedband AMR is different, and it might still have current patent protection, which seems to be an issue for the wireshark team in the past.  I personally would have a different assessment (as the codec is not in wireshark but an optional third party library).  But that's off-topich here, so let's please keep this patch/PR on traditional AMR (later called narrow band) only.

This patch implements the kind of SDP which is specified in RFC4867 which uses a syntax like "rtpmap:97 AMR/8000/1".  This is also what is used in 2G/GSM cellular networks, see TS 48.103

For 3G/UMTS networks, there is no AMR inside RTP, but there is the intermediate IuFP layer.  The original transport was AMR over ATM, and the IP/RTP encapsulation was added later.  The specs state that most fields of the RTP header are to be ignored, and all of the relevant information is in the IuFP header carried inside RTP.  And inside IuFP there's then AMR.  Whether or not this codec is called from within IuFP I don't know, but it's an independent question for the IuFP dissector, and not one of the codec here.

If 4G/VoLTE/VoWiFi/IMS sytems use "AMR-NB" in the SDP (which I find rather odd) would be worth citing a related spec.  The same cocdec could then be registered both for AMR and for "AMR-NB".  I'd also put that question into a follow-up patch.  

Let's get this merged first, supporting RC4867 and GSM/2G networks, and do anything else incrementally.
If you look at [VoiceAge's claims](https://voiceage.com/Patent-Portfolio.html), they don't claim any patents on AMR-WB past 2024. (AMR-WB+ they claim a few that expire later in the US and Brazil.)

@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+# Find the system's opencore-amrnb includes and library
+#
+#  AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIRS - where to find amrnb/decoder.h
+#  AMRNB_LIBRARIES    - List of libraries when using amrnb
+#  AMRNB_FOUND        - True if amrnb found
+#  AMRNB_DLL_DIR      - (Windows) Path to the amrnb DLL
+#  AMRNB_DLL          - (Windows) Name of the amrnb DLL
+
+include( FindWSWinLibs )
+FindWSWinLibs( "opencore-amrnb-.*" "AMRNB_HINTS" )
+
+if (NOT WIN32)
+  find_package(PkgConfig)
+  pkg_search_module(AMRNB opencore-amrnb)
+endif()
+
+find_path( AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIR
+  NAMES opencore-amrnb/interf_dec.h
+  HINTS
+    "${AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIR}"
+    "${AMRNB_HINTS}/include"
+  PATHS /usr/local/include /usr/include
+)
+
+find_library( AMRNB_LIBRARY
+  NAMES opencore-amrnb
+  HINTS
+    "${AMRNB_LIBDIR}"
+    "${AMRNB_HINTS}/lib"
+  PATHS /usr/local/lib /usr/lib
+)
+
+include( FindPackageHandleStandardArgs )
+find_package_handle_standard_args( amrnb DEFAULT_MSG AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIR AMRNB_LIBRARY )
+
+if( AMRNB_FOUND )
+  set( AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIRS ${AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIR} )
+  set( AMRNB_LIBRARIES ${AMRNB_LIBRARY} )
+  if (WIN32)
+    set ( AMRNB_DLL_DIR "${AMRNB_HINTS}/bin"
+      CACHE PATH "Path to amrnb DLL"
+    )
+    file( GLOB _amrnb_dll RELATIVE "${AMRNB_DLL_DIR}"
+      "${AMRNB_DLL_DIR}/libamrnb.dll"
+    )
+    set ( AMRNB_DLL ${_amrnb_dll}
+      # We're storing filenames only. Should we use STRING instead?
+      CACHE FILEPATH "amrnb DLL file name"
+    )
+    mark_as_advanced( AMRNB_DLL_DIR AMRNB_DLL )
+  endif()
+else()
+  set( AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIRS )
+  set( AMRNB_LIBRARIES )
+endif()
+
+mark_as_advanced( AMRNB_LIBRARIES AMRNB_INCLUDE_DIRS )
